docs.text: Driver TMC9660 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the TMC9660 servo controller and gate driver: the bootloader, parameter mode and register mode, over SPI or UART, with guards so that nothing energises a motor by accident. It runs on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the frames of three protocols, the checks of every reply, the parameter and register tables, and the rules that keep the power stage off until the chip and your request say otherwise. The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/tmc9660.hpp public calls ; inc/tmc9660_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; inc/tmc9660_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you get ¶ Three modes in one class. Mode::Bootloader , Mode::Parameter and Mode::Register ; a call that belongs to another mode returns WrongMode and sends nothing. See Bootloader , Parameter mode and Register mode . Checked tables. All 289 parameters and 163 registers of the reference manuals, with access, range and coded values; a bad value is refused before a byte leaves. Safe to start and to stop. EnableDrive() reads the flags and raises DRV_EN before it sets the commutation mode; DisableDrive() is never refused. See Safety . Reset-aware. The driver watches each transport for evidence that the chip restarted and sends no write after it. Explicit where the documents disagree. Twenty-four ambiguities (A1 to A24), most with a knob. See Ambiguities . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against an independent model of the chip, a fuzz target attacks it, and one-edit mutants of every guard must be caught. See Testing and CI . Not yet run on a real chip Everything is verified against a model built from the documents. The ambiguities page lists what a bench check should settle first. Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, read a parameter in about 15 lines. Hardware Pins, bus settings, timing and power. Safety What keeps the power stage off, and what the driver does not cover. Contract What the driver promises, what it needs, threading and errors. docs.text: Ambiguities and unverified items ¶ The three TMC9660 documents (datasheet, Parameter Mode Reference Manual, Register Mode Reference Manual) disagree with each other in places, or leave a detail open. For each, the driver reads the documents one way by default and a knob in Config or Quirks selects the other reading, so a bench check can settle it without a code change. The frame encoders are proved against the documents' worked examples with static_assert . Id The documents Default reading Knob A1 Bootloader CRC-8: the prose reflects the output, the worked examples ( 0x1D , 0xA3 ) do not Not reflected Quirks::crc8_reflect_output A2 TMCL: where the type bits [11:8] sit in the byte shared with the motor number: the manual's bit table puts the motor number in the high nibble, a vendor example the other way Auto : probed at start, refuses if both or neither layout answers (fail closed) Quirks::tmcl_layout ( Auto , MotorHigh , TypeHigh ) A3 Register SPI: a 9-bit offset in the table, registers up to 0x208 , and a RAMDebug example with 10 bits Table layout; offsets above 0x1FF return Unsupported Quirks::reg_spi_wide_offset A4 Register UART: order of the fields in a datagram Table order, block in the top 5 bits of byte 3 Quirks::reg_uart_msb_fields A5 TMCL SPI: what to do on NOT_READY or CHECKSUM_ERROR Repeat only the reply request, up to the retry count Config::spi_reply_retries A6 TMCL UART: the gap that discards a partial message, 100 ms or 10 ms 100 ms assumed; the resync waits uart_resync_us (150 ms, a 50 % margin) before it drains; a port must not pause more than 10 ms inside a frame Config::reply_timeout_us (and your port) A7 Parameter mode has no reset flag in a UART reply A canary variable written at start and read before each write (UART); Service() also reads GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS and treats a WATCHDOG_EVENT that was not set at the start as a restart (a watchdog reset only; a power-on reset sets no flag the driver knows of, and the driver never clears the word) Config::uart_canary , canary_variable , canary_value A8 Parameter 165: range 1 to 8, reset value 0 The reset value is accepted, the range is enforced for other writes the model accepts 0 A9 T_WAKE is given as a typical value only boot_timeout_ms is 500 and bounds the identity wait (after a pin reset the driver first waits 50 ms): each failed poll is charged its pause and, on UART, its reply wait and resync (see Configuration ) Config::boot_timeout_ms A10 ABN2_B offset printed as 32, probably 34 34 raw BootConfig::SetWord() A11 The version string has no usual checksum GetInfo is used for the identity none A12 BL_UART_RX text mentions the "TX pin" Read as RX none A13 The Boot reply is sent before the new configuration applies The reply is read, then the driver waits Config::settle_us A14 Errata 2 and 6 need explicit values; erratum 5 may cut the host link Never applied automatically; DisableSpi1Slave() is an explicit call none A15 Which flags forbid starting Any non-zero GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS or GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS ; a warning bit therefore also stops EnableDrive() (stricter than needed) none: clear the flags first A16 SPI encoder chip-select polarity printed as bit 19 of a 16-bit word Not exposed as a typed field raw BootConfig::SetWord() A17 RAMDebug index width: 5 bits (bit ranges) or 6 (offset example 640) 5 Quirks::ram_debug_index_bits A18 FAULTN low in an application: a reset or a fault Not a reset. With faultn_is_reset set, a gate-driver fault that pulls FAULTN low makes every register-UART write, including the write that clears the fault, return UnexpectedReset and uninitialise the driver; the stop is never gated by it Config::faultn_is_reset A20 Register mode: the reset value of GDRV_HW is printed as 0x03300FFF in the manual's text and 0x03000FFF in its register table The table ( 0x03000FFF ); the driver never relies on the reset value none A21 TMCL SPI reply: the reply layout is given as a table and as prose that differ in the position of the status byte The table: status, module, command, value none ( TmclSpiRequest is the same either way) A22 GetInfo type 0 (ID): the format of the value is not given Compared with the chip ID 0x544D0001 none A23 Bootloader SPI Table 3: the literal byte layout Request command, value[4] , reply status, value[4] , as the worked examples none A24 Bootloader: whether writing the boot-mode word starts the application on a 0-to-1 change of START_MOTOR_CTRL or on any write with the bit set (the datasheet, "Launching Applications", p. 76, says only that the manually triggered sequence "is run when the boot configuration register is written to"), and whether the bootloader shows the bit set after Boot from an auto-started application (datasheet Figures 32, 34, 35) Any write of the word with the bit set is treated as a start: the driver follows it and falls back to the bootloader when that still answers none A19 UART reply time: neither manual bounds the time from the last request byte to the first reply byte 1 ms assumed kTurnaroundUs (a port reads it; the driver itself waits on the port) Not verified ¶ These are open because the documents do not settle them and no real chip has been available: The format of GetInfo type 0 in parameter mode (the driver compares it with the chip ID; Config has no knob). The SPI parameter-mode frame laid out literally as in PM Table 3 (type in bits 8 to 19 and motor in bits 20 to 23 of the 32-bit word, MSB first, so type[11:4] in byte 1) is not supported (A2): a read-only probe decodes type 299 as 0x2B0, the chip answers an error to both probes, and the start is refused with nothing written. Supporting it needs a code change (a third TmclLayout ); it is a bench item. UART is not affected. The nibble order (A2) is probed at start-up and refused when it does not decide; which of the two layouts the chip uses, whether it ignores the motor nibble, and the register offset width and UART field order (A3, A4) are bench items, and so is what a parameter-mode stop does when it reaches a register-mode chip over SPI (the frame lands on block 1 offset 9 and block 63 offset 0x100 in the table layout, on MCC 0x104, 0x109 and 0x22b or RAMDebug 0x300 in the wide one). Whether GDRV_STATUS_EN = 0 stops the status from latching, which status bits latch at power-up, and how long the bootstrap capacitors need before the protection words are written are bench items ( settle_us is used). The UART reply time (A19) is an assumption. Register-mode UART and bootloader UART have no reset evidence in their replies; only FAULTN can show an unseen reset, and only when your port has GpioGet() . WATCHDOG_EVENT is a read-write-clear flag the driver does not clear: a chip adopted with it already set cannot show a new watchdog reset through that flag (UART still has the canary, SPI the FIRST_CMD status). Whether IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR 0 on a real stage keeps the outputs driven after COMMUTATION_MODE 0 as the manual says is a bench item; the driver treats it as written. Whether scripts on the chip can energise the stage: the driver refuses only SAP and AAP of COMMUTATION_MODE in a downloaded script ( Refused ); it does not analyse anything else, and ScriptRun() starts whatever the chip already holds. The meaning of every bit of the warning subset of the flag parameters. The parameter-mode GetStatus type value (0 assumed). The numbering of the SIO and GIO pins for SetIo() and GetIo() . The Verify trailing arguments that other drivers of the family have are not implemented here: writes are checked by the chip's reply and, for the configuration, by reading back. One corrupted status byte on SPI can hide FIRST_CMD (see Safety ). readParamRaw ignores its guarded argument for reads; reads never energise anything. The ESP32 example is compiled against a stub of ESP-IDF only; a build with the real SDK is pending. The MISRA C++:2023 scan (CodeQL) runs in CI, not in this host build. When you settle one on a bench, report it: the change is a default and a changelog line.

docs.text: API guide ¶ The calls of the driver, task by task. Every call returns Result<T> : check ok() before you use value . Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Bootloader commands and reply status codes: Bootloader, Commands, p. 76 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Start ¶ tmc9660 :: Error BringUp ( Chip & chip ) { // The one entry point: starts on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a failure the // next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "TMC9660 init: %s \n " , tmc9660 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } EnsureInitialized() is the only call that starts the driver; it returns Ok with no I/O once it has succeeded. It checks the identity of the chip in the mode named by Config::mode . The chip is not reset unless you set Config::hardware_reset . After a failure the next call starts again. Start the application from the bootloader ¶ tmc9660 :: Error StartApplication ( Chip & chip ) { // The chip comes up in its bootloader. Read the configuration, change one field, write it back: // only the words that differ are written, the boot-mode word last, and the driver refuses a start // that would hang the chip. auto cfg = chip . BlReadConfig (); if ( ! cfg ) { return cfg . error ; } tmc9660 :: BootConfig next = cfg . value ; if ( const auto e = next . Set ( tmc9660 :: BootField :: BootMode , 2U ); e != tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ) { return e ; // 2 is parameter mode } if ( const auto e = next . Set ( tmc9660 :: BootField :: StartMotorCtrl , 1U ); e != tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ) { return e ; } return chip . BlWriteConfig ( next ). error ; // follows the chip into parameter mode } A freshly powered chip is in its bootloader ( Mode::Bootloader ). BlWriteConfig() writes only the words that differ, the boot-mode word last, verifies by reading back, and follows the chip into the new mode. It refuses a start that would use a reserved boot mode or a clock other than 40 MHz, and a change of the LDO outputs unless you allow it. BlStartApplication(BootMode::Parameter) does the same in one call. More in Bootloader . Set and read parameters ¶ tmc9660 :: Error SetLimits ( Chip & chip ) { // Every parameter is checked against the datasheet's range and coded set before a byte is sent. if ( auto r = chip . SetParam ( tmc9660 :: Param :: MOTOR_TYPE , 3 ); ! r ) { // 3: BLDC; needs the system off return r . error ; } if ( auto r = chip . SetParam ( tmc9660 :: Param :: MAX_TORQUE , 1500 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // InvalidArgument above 65535: nothing was sent } return chip . StoreParams (). error ; } SetParam() and GetParam() check the parameter against Table 57 first: access, range, coded values and the motor number. StoreParams() saves the settings in the chip's external memory. More in Parameter mode . Drive the motor ¶ tmc9660 :: Error RunMotor ( Chip & chip ) { // The only way to a non-zero commutation mode. The guards read the flag words first; DRV_EN rises // only after they are clean, then the mode is set. if ( auto r = chip . EnableDrive ( 3 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // DeviceFault: an error flag is latched; Refused is never returned here } const auto r = chip . SetTargetVelocity ( 500 ); if ( ! r ) { static_cast < void > ( chip . DisableDrive ()); // never refused: DRV_EN first, then the commutation mode return r . error ; } return tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ; } EnableDrive(mode) is the only way to a non-zero commutation mode: it reads the error flags ( DeviceFault if one is set), raises DRV_EN and only then writes the mode. DisableDrive() drops DRV_EN, then writes mode 0, and is never refused; Deinitialize() does the same stop before it forgets the chip. See Safety . Register mode ¶ tmc9660 :: Error StartGateDriver ( Chip & chip ) { // Register mode: the gate driver starts only through GateDriverStart(), which runs the manual's // sequence with the fault and undervoltage guards before the energising write. WriteReg() refuses // those bits. tmc9660 :: GateDriverRegConfig cfg {}; cfg . gdrv_cfg = 0x0003'0000U ; // gate currents and adaptive mode: see the register reference return chip . GateDriverStart ( cfg ). error ; } ReadReg() , WriteReg() and UpdateReg() work on the 163 registers; ReadField() and WriteField() take a fields::<register>::<Field> type. GateDriverStart() runs the manual's start sequence with the fault guards before the energising write, and the energising bits are refused anywhere else. See Register mode . Notice a reset ¶ tmc9660 :: Error KeepAlive ( Chip & chip ) { const auto r = chip . Service (); // FAULTN and a heartbeat read: the way to notice a reset if ( r . error == tmc9660 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset ) { static_cast < void > ( chip . DisableDrive ()); // the pin first return chip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // the chip lost its configuration: start it again } return r . error ; } A reset of the chip loses its configuration and, in parameter mode, the drive settings. The driver watches each transport for evidence (the status byte on SPI, the canary variable on UART, the boot bit and counter in register mode) and returns UnexpectedReset instead of sending a write that might act on a chip it no longer knows. Call Service() from your main loop: it reads FAULTN when the port has GpioGet() and Config::faultn_is_reset is set, and polls one status parameter in parameter mode. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( tmc9660 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case tmc9660 :: Error :: Bus : case tmc9660 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check the bus wiring, the mode and the device address" ; case tmc9660 :: Error :: WrongMode : return "the chip is in another mode: nothing was sent" ; case tmc9660 :: Error :: Refused : return "a safety guard said no: read the documentation of the call" ; case tmc9660 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset : return "the chip restarted: call EnsureInitialized() again" ; default : return tmc9660 :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring; retry, or Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() Error::Timeout No reply, or the PLL did not lock Check VCC_IO and RSTN; raise boot_timeout_ms or reply_timeout_us Error::DeviceIdMismatch The chip ID is wrong Check the mode, the device address and the wiring Error::Crc , Error::BadReply A reply was corrupted on the bus Lower the bus clock; check grounding; the value was discarded Error::Busy The bootloader stayed busy Retry after a delay; raise spi_reply_retries Error::DeviceFault An error flag is latched Read and clear the flags after fixing the cause Error::Nack The chip refused the command LastStatus() has the chip's status code Error::WrongMode The call belongs to another mode Nothing was sent; start the right mode Error::Refused A safety guard said no Read the guard on Safety ; nothing was changed Error::VerifyFailed A read back differed The chip did not take the write; do not start the application Error::UnexpectedReset The chip restarted EnsureInitialized() , then configure again Error::Unsupported An offset or hook this setup cannot reach See A3 or add the GpioSet() hook Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. tmc9660::ToString() names an error for a log. Diagnostics ¶ Call I/O What it gives IsInitialized() none Whether the driver is started GetMode() none The mode the driver speaks LastStatus() none The status code of the last reply (TMCL status, bootloader status, register-mode flag) GetLastReply() none Status, command number and value of the last valid parameter-mode reply ReadRawParam() one command A GAP with a parameter number taken as given; the unsigned reply value; nothing is written GetConfig() none The configuration in use GetChipId() , GetVersion() one command The chip ID and version (parameter mode); BlGetInfo() in the bootloader Shut down ¶ void PowerDown ( Chip & chip ) { if ( auto r = chip . docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error BringUp ( Chip & chip ) { // The one entry point: starts on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a failure the // next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "TMC9660 init: %s \n " , tmc9660 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } EnsureInitialized() is the only call that starts the driver; it returns Ok with no I/O once it has succeeded. It checks the identity of the chip in the mode named by Config::mode . The chip is not reset unless you set Config::hardware_reset . After a failure the next call starts again.
docs.title: Start

docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error StartApplication ( Chip & chip ) { // The chip comes up in its bootloader. Read the configuration, change one field, write it back: // only the words that differ are written, the boot-mode word last, and the driver refuses a start // that would hang the chip. auto cfg = chip . BlReadConfig (); if ( ! cfg ) { return cfg . error ; } tmc9660 :: BootConfig next = cfg . value ; if ( const auto e = next . Set ( tmc9660 :: BootField :: BootMode , 2U ); e != tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ) { return e ; // 2 is parameter mode } if ( const auto e = next . Set ( tmc9660 :: BootField :: StartMotorCtrl , 1U ); e != tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ) { return e ; } return chip . BlWriteConfig ( next ). error ; // follows the chip into parameter mode } A freshly powered chip is in its bootloader ( Mode::Bootloader ). BlWriteConfig() writes only the words that differ, the boot-mode word last, verifies by reading back, and follows the chip into the new mode. It refuses a start that would use a reserved boot mode or a clock other than 40 MHz, and a change of the LDO outputs unless you allow it. BlStartApplication(BootMode::Parameter) does the same in one call. More in Bootloader .
docs.title: Start the application from the bootloader

docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error SetLimits ( Chip & chip ) { // Every parameter is checked against the datasheet's range and coded set before a byte is sent. if ( auto r = chip . SetParam ( tmc9660 :: Param :: MOTOR_TYPE , 3 ); ! r ) { // 3: BLDC; needs the system off return r . error ; } if ( auto r = chip . SetParam ( tmc9660 :: Param :: MAX_TORQUE , 1500 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // InvalidArgument above 65535: nothing was sent } return chip . StoreParams (). error ; } SetParam() and GetParam() check the parameter against Table 57 first: access, range, coded values and the motor number. StoreParams() saves the settings in the chip's external memory. More in Parameter mode .
docs.title: Set and read parameters

docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error RunMotor ( Chip & chip ) { // The only way to a non-zero commutation mode. The guards read the flag words first; DRV_EN rises // only after they are clean, then the mode is set. if ( auto r = chip . EnableDrive ( 3 ); ! r ) { return r . error ; // DeviceFault: an error flag is latched; Refused is never returned here } const auto r = chip . SetTargetVelocity ( 500 ); if ( ! r ) { static_cast < void > ( chip . DisableDrive ()); // never refused: DRV_EN first, then the commutation mode return r . error ; } return tmc9660 :: Error :: Ok ; } EnableDrive(mode) is the only way to a non-zero commutation mode: it reads the error flags ( DeviceFault if one is set), raises DRV_EN and only then writes the mode. DisableDrive() drops DRV_EN, then writes mode 0, and is never refused; Deinitialize() does the same stop before it forgets the chip. See Safety .
docs.title: Drive the motor

docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error StartGateDriver ( Chip & chip ) { // Register mode: the gate driver starts only through GateDriverStart(), which runs the manual's // sequence with the fault and undervoltage guards before the energising write. WriteReg() refuses // those bits. tmc9660 :: GateDriverRegConfig cfg {}; cfg . gdrv_cfg = 0x0003'0000U ; // gate currents and adaptive mode: see the register reference return chip . GateDriverStart ( cfg ). error ; } ReadReg() , WriteReg() and UpdateReg() work on the 163 registers; ReadField() and WriteField() take a fields::<register>::<Field> type. GateDriverStart() runs the manual's start sequence with the fault guards before the energising write, and the energising bits are refused anywhere else. See Register mode .
docs.title: Register mode

docs.text: tmc9660 :: Error KeepAlive ( Chip & chip ) { const auto r = chip . Service (); // FAULTN and a heartbeat read: the way to notice a reset if ( r . error == tmc9660 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset ) { static_cast < void > ( chip . DisableDrive ()); // the pin first return chip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // the chip lost its configuration: start it again } return r . error ; } A reset of the chip loses its configuration and, in parameter mode, the drive settings. The driver watches each transport for evidence (the status byte on SPI, the canary variable on UART, the boot bit and counter in register mode) and returns UnexpectedReset instead of sending a write that might act on a chip it no longer knows. Call Service() from your main loop: it reads FAULTN when the port has GpioGet() and Config::faultn_is_reset is set, and polls one status parameter in parameter mode.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built, so you can read the code, add a feature or port it. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Application modes: Application Modes, p. 16 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Layers ¶ The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/tmc9660.hpp public calls ; inc/tmc9660_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; inc/tmc9660_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The core, tmc9660::TMC9660<Port> , has no platform code. It calls hooks on your port class, which derives from SpiInterface<Port> or from UartInterface<Port> . The concept AnyPort accepts exactly one of the two, checked at compile time. Files ¶ File Contents inc/tmc9660.hpp , src/tmc9660.ipp The class: lifecycle, the three modes, the safety guards inc/tmc9660_types.hpp Error , Result , Mode , Config , Quirks , enumerations inc/tmc9660_frames.hpp Pure frame encoders and decoders of all protocols, proved with static_assert inc/tmc9660_bootconfig.hpp BootConfig and the field table of the configuration memory inc/tmc9660_params.hpp The 289 parameters (generated) inc/tmc9660_registers.hpp The 163 registers and their bit fields (generated) inc/tmc9660_globals.hpp The global parameters of the four banks inc/tmc9660_spi_interface.hpp , inc/tmc9660_uart_interface.hpp The port contracts and the bus requirements inc/tmc9660_kconfig.hpp KconfigDefaults() for ESP-IDF menuconfig The .ipp file is included at the end of tmc9660.hpp : the driver is header-only. One class, three modes ¶ The chip speaks one of three protocols, and which one depends on its boot configuration, so the mode is a run-time value ( Mode ), not a template parameter. Every public function starts with need(Mode) : a call in the wrong mode returns WrongMode before it touches the bus. A change of mode, by BlStartApplication() , BlWriteConfig() or ReturnToBootloader() , updates mode_ after the chip identity has been read in the new mode. Transport and protocol are separate ¶ Frames are built and parsed by detail:: functions in tmc9660_frames.hpp : no I/O, no state, constexpr , each proved against the documents' worked examples. The class owns the exchange: send the frame, check the reply, track the reset evidence of that transport ( FIRST_CMD , the boot bit and datagram counter, the canary), map the result to Error . That is why a protocol detail is a unit test of a pure function and the exchange logic is a test against the chip model. Generated tables ¶ The parameter and register tables are generated from tools/gen_tables/params.json and regs.json , which were transcribed from the reference manuals, by tools/gen_tables/gen_tables.py . The output is formatted with the repository's clang-format and a CTest checks that the committed headers equal the generator's output ( Testing ). The model ¶ tests/mock_tmc9660.hpp is an independent model of the chip, written from the documents and not from the driver: it has the three protocols, the parameter and register tables, memories, reset, and the faults of the chip as switches. It records what happened to the chip (writes after a reset, energise events with an error flag latched or DRV_EN low, boot with the drive on) so that a test asserts on the chip, not on the driver's own opinion.

docs.text: Bootloader ¶ After power-up the TMC9660 runs its bootloader. It answers on UART and on SPI at the same time, holds a 64-byte configuration (16 little-endian words) and starts the motion-control application in parameter mode or register mode when that configuration says so. The driver exposes the bootloader as Mode::Bootloader : the Bl* calls. Datasheet sections this page relies on UART bootloader frame and its CRC-8: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Bootloader, UART Communication, p. 70 SPI bootloader frame and delayed reply: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Bootloader, SPI Communication, p. 72 Bootloader commands and reply status codes: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Bootloader, Commands, p. 76 Boot configuration list, LDO and bootstrap configuration: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Bootloader, Configuration, p. 83 Errata (OTP_BURN workaround, SPI slave MISO): Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Errata, p. 99 Bootstrapping with the UblTools software: Analog Devices (Trinamic) AN-2601 0, Bootstrapping the TMC9660 IC using UblTools, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Frames ¶ Bus Request Reply Driver UART 8 bytes: 0x55 , device address, command, type, value (4 bytes), CRC-8 8 bytes in the same layout with the host address, a status and the CRC-8 Exchange() , one call per frame SPI 5 bytes: command, value (4 bytes) The reply to a command comes with the next transfer; a NO_OP fetches it Transfer() , two or more per command The CRC-8 uses polynomial 0x07 , start value 0, input bytes reflected. Whether the result is reflected too is ambiguity A1: the prose says yes and the worked examples say no. The driver follows the examples and proves them with static_assert in inc/tmc9660_frames.hpp ; Quirks::crc8_reflect_output selects the other reading. On SPI the status of a reply can be BUSY (the chip is still working). The driver repeats the NO_OP fetch up to Config::spi_reply_retries times and then returns Error::Busy ; it never repeats the command itself, because a write must not run twice. SESSION_START (19) and BOOTLOADER_RESUMED (21) in a status tell the driver that the chip restarted since the last frame: it returns Error::UnexpectedReset and sends nothing else until EnsureInitialized() ran again. Calls ¶ Call What it does Guards BlGetInfo(BlInfo) GET_INFO : chip type, bootloader version, clock, memory sizes WrongMode outside the bootloader BlRead32(Bank, address) Reads a word from SPI flash, I2C EEPROM, OTP or the configuration memory Address must be a multiple of 4 BlWrite32(Bank, address, value) Writes a word to SPI flash or I2C EEPROM Refused for the OTP bank and for the configuration memory BlReadConfig() Reads the 64 bytes into a typed BootConfig BlWriteConfig(config, options) Writes a configuration and verifies it See below BlStartApplication(BootMode) Sets BOOT_MODE and START_MOTOR_CTRL , writes, follows the chip into the new mode Refused for a reserved mode BlMemoryStatus(Bank, MemQuery) MEM_IS_CONFIGURED , MEM_IS_CONNECTED , MEM_IS_BUSY BlEraseFlashSector(address) FLASH_ERASE_SECTOR Refused unless the flash is configured, connected and idle BlOtpLoad() OTP_LOAD : load the OTP configuration OTP_BURN is not exposed: it is permanent, and the datasheet's erratum 1 needs a multi-step workaround. Writing to the OTP bank through BlWrite32() is Refused . If you need to burn the OTP, use the vendor's tool. Writing a configuration ¶ BootConfig has one named field for every documented option ( BootField ), range checked, with the layout in a single table. A field the documents leave unclear, such as the polarity of the SPI encoder's chip select (A16), is reached through the raw SetWord() . BlWriteConfig() is built to refuse the configurations that are known to leave the chip in a state the board did not ask for (the checks below are the ones the documents allow; a configuration the documents do not describe is not judged): It refuses, before writing anything, a configuration that would start the application with a reserved boot mode or with a system clock other than 40 MHz ( BootConfig::CheckStart() ), and a change of the LDO word unless BlWriteOptions::allow_ldo_change is set (both outputs VEXT1 and VEXT2 move at once). It writes only the words that differ, the clock word with one 32-bit write, and the boot-mode word last. After a clock change it waits for the PLL to lock ( Error::Timeout if it does not) and reads every word back ( Error::VerifyFailed on a difference, the lock status bit excepted). If the write starts the application, it checks that the PLL is locked first, then switches the driver to the new mode and checks the chip ID there. BlStartApplication(target) is BlReadConfig() , two field changes and BlWriteConfig() . Returning to the bootloader ¶ ReturnToBootloader() (parameter mode) sends the Boot command. Erratum 3 of the Parameter Mode Reference Manual says that exiting to the bootloader with the motor running can leave the gate driver on, so the driver switches the drive off first, reads COMMUTATION_MODE back, and sends nothing if it is not zero ( Error::Refused ). See Safety . Erratum 3 of the Parameter Mode Reference Manual says that exiting to the bootloader with the motor running can leave the gate driver on, so the driver switches the drive off first, reads COMMUTATION_MODE back, and sends nothing if it is not zero ( Error::Refused ). See Safety . Document Revision Get it Datasheet: TMC9660 70V Smart Gate Driver with Servo (FOC) Controller in HW and Buck Converter (Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926) 1, 2024-11 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Parameter Mode Reference Manual (Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a) 0, 2025-02 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Register Mode Reference Manual (Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a) 0, 2025-04 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Configuration and Bootstrapping (Analog Devices (Trinamic) AN-2601) 0, 2025-01-08 vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ TMC9660 driver, first version: the bootloader (information, memory, typed configuration, guarded application start, flash erase), parameter mode (289 checked parameters, global parameters, scripts, RAMDebug, I/O) and register mode (163 checked registers, fields, RAMDebug, guarded gate-driver start), over SPI or UART. Safety guards: the drive is enabled only through EnableDrive() and GateDriverStart() after the error flags are read, DisableDrive() is never refused, no write follows a reset the driver saw, and the OTP is never written. Documented ambiguities (A1 to A24), most with a configuration knob ( Config , Quirks ). Quirks::tmcl_layout ( Auto , MotorHigh , TypeHigh ): the TMCL byte layout is probed with two reads at start-up and the start is refused when it is not decided; Config::uart_resync_us : the gap after a failed UART exchange before the line is drained. GateDriverStart() writes GDRV_PROT , GDRV_OCP_UVW , GDRV_OCP_Y2 , GDRV_STATUS_EN and GDRV_PROT_EN ( GateDriverRegConfig::gdrv_prot , gdrv_ocp_uvw , gdrv_ocp_y2 , status_en , prot_en ) and reads the latched status before clearing it. Config::allow_pwm_in_system_off : SetParam(IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR, 0) is Refused without it, and the stop of a port with no DRV_EN hook sets the parameter to 1 (PM "System Off") and fails rather than return Ok with the PWM active. A stop is sent before a UART line is resynchronised, a failed register-mode stop write is repeated once, and GateDriverStart() reads the latched evidence again after the protections are on ( DeviceFault on a trip). PowerDown() and ReturnToBootloader() return UnexpectedReset and send nothing after their stop when the stop saw a reset (found by the fuzz gate: PowerDown() returned NotInitialized after sending, ReturnToBootloader() sent Boot ). A UART drain that fails leaves the line dirty and the call returns Bus without sending (a stale reply could answer the next read). The fuzz target's reset promise now follows the driver's current mode. The parameter-mode stop and MotorStop() are sent once more after any failure, not only after a reported reset (the repeat resynchronises a dirty UART line first); a failed EnableDrive() runs the full stop of DisableDrive() , so it leaves the drive stopped also without a DRV_EN hook. A failed EnsureInitialized() keeps the protocol the driver last proved, so a stop after a failed restart still reaches a started application; without a proved protocol in bootloader mode and without a DRV_EN hook, DisableDrive() returns NotInitialized instead of Ok . Config::uart_resync_us is now 150 ms (50 % over the chip's discard gap, A6). A start of the application from the bootloader whose write fails other than by a bootloader error status, or any write of the boot-mode word with START_MOTOR_CTRL set (A24), is followed as a start, so a later stop reaches the application. With the bootloader adopted and no DRV_EN hook, DisableDrive() is Ok only when the bootloader still answers. The identity wait after a reset, a start or Boot is bounded by boot_timeout_ms : each failed UART poll is charged its reply wait, resync gap and drains. In bootloader mode without a DRV_EN hook, a stop that finds no bootloader sends the stop of the application the last BOOT_MODE read named (or Config::mode ) and leaves the driver uninitialised in that protocol. docs/deviations.yml : the repository's (empty) deviation record file, read by the MISRA workflow. BlEraseFlashSector(address, allow_partition_table) checks alignment and range and refuses sector 0 unless asked. Service() sees a WATCHDOG_EVENT as a restart in parameter mode. tools/gen_tables/extract_check.py : re-derives the table counts from the manuals' text. The generator of the parameter and register tables ( tools/gen_tables ), the model-based tests, a fuzz target and the mutation tool ( tools/mutants ). Documentation: hardware figures and tables, bootloader, parameter mode, register mode, safety, ambiguities, coverage of the chip's features.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Config is the whole configuration of the driver; Config{} is the chip's reset configuration. Nothing in it is written to the chip: it says how the driver talks and waits. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Boot configuration list, LDO and bootstrap configuration: Bootloader, Configuration, p. 83 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Fields ¶ Field Default Range What it does mode Mode::Parameter Bootloader , Parameter , Register The protocol the chip is in at EnsureInitialized() device_address 1 1 to 255, odd for TMCL and register mode on UART The UART device address (the upper 7 bits are the TMCL address) host_address 255 1 to 255 Host address in bootloader UART replies tmcl_host_address 2 1 to 255 Host address in TMCL and register-mode UART replies reply_timeout_us 50 000 1 or more How long the UART port waits for a reply boot_timeout_ms 500 1 or more Bounds every identity wait after a reset, a start or Boot (A9). Each failed poll is charged the 10 ms pause and, on UART, the longest it can take: reply_timeout_us , uart_resync_us and three 5 ms drains (225 ms with the defaults), so a chip that never answers is given up after about boot_timeout_ms plus one poll: two or three polls on UART, 50 on SPI settle_us 20 000 Wait after a write that reconfigures the chip (A13) spi_gap_us 1 000 Gap between a TMCL SPI command and its reply request spi_reply_retries 5 0 to 50 Repeats of the reply request on NOT_READY or CHECKSUM_ERROR (A5) uart_canary true Parameter mode over UART: detect an unseen reset (A7) canary_variable 15 0 to 15 The user variable that holds the canary canary_value 0x5AC3A55A The canary hardware_reset false needs GpioSet() Pulse RSTN at start instead of adopting the chip, then wait 50 ms (T_WAKE is 44 ms typical, A9) before the first identity poll; that wait is not charged to boot_timeout_ms faultn_is_reset false needs GpioGet() Service() treats FAULTN low outside the bootloader as a reset (A18) allow_pwm_in_system_off false Allow SetParam(IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR, 0) (the PWM stays active in System off). The stop of a port without a DRV_EN hook sets the parameter to 1 whatever this says uart_resync_us 150 000 The gap after a failed UART exchange before the line is drained: the chip's discard gap of about 100 ms (A6) with a 50 % margin; a stop is sent before it quirks see below Readings of ambiguous documentation tmc9660 :: Config UartConfig () { tmc9660 :: Config c {}; // the defaults c . mode = tmc9660 :: Mode :: Parameter ; c . device_address = 3 ; // UART: odd, as set in the boot configuration c . boot_timeout_ms = 750 ; // how long to wait for the chip after a reset c . uart_canary = true ; // detect an unseen reset through a user variable return c ; // tmc9660::Validate(c) checks it without the chip } tmc9660 :: Error StartOnUart ( MyUartPort & port ) { static tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MyUartPort > chip ( port , UartConfig ()); // stored, no I/O return chip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // InvalidArgument if the config is out of range } Readings of ambiguous documents ¶ Where the documents disagree the driver reads them one way by default; Quirks selects the other ( Ambiguities ): Field Default Ambiguity crc8_reflect_output false A1: the bootloader CRC-8 output reflection tmcl_layout Auto A2: the type bits of a TMCL frame; Auto probes with two reads, MotorHigh or TypeHigh is verified the same way reg_spi_wide_offset false A3: 9-bit or 10-bit register offset on SPI reg_uart_msb_fields false A4: field order of register UART datagrams ram_debug_index_bits 5 A17: 5 or 6 tmc9660 :: Config RegisterModeWithOtherReadings () { tmc9660 :: Config c {}; c . mode = tmc9660 :: Mode :: Register ; c . quirks . reg_spi_wide_offset = true ; // ambiguity A3: the other reading of the register datagram layout c . quirks . ram_debug_index_bits = 6 ; // ambiguity A17: a 6-bit RAMDebug index return c ; } Validation ¶ tmc9660::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() calls it before any I/O. It returns Error::InvalidArgument when mode is not an enumerator, an address, timeout or the canary variable is out of range, or ram_debug_index_bits is not 5 or 6. EnsureInitialized() also rejects an even device address on UART in parameter or register mode, and hardware_reset without a GpioSet() hook ( Unsupported ). A configuration can be proven at build time, so that a wrong one does not compile: // A configuration proven at build time: an invalid one does not compile. constexpr tmc9660 :: CheckedConfig kBoardConfig { tmc9660 :: Config {. mode = tmc9660 :: Mode :: Register }}; tmc9660 :: Mode BoardMode () { return kBoardConfig . Get (). mode ; } Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows TMC9660 servo controller when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options reach the code only through inc/tmc9660_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: tmc9660 :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MyPort > chip ( port , tmc9660 :: KconfigDefaults ()); return chip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Option Default Config field CONFIG_TMC9660_MODE_* Parameter mode mode CONFIG_TMC9660_DEVICE_ADDRESS 1 device_address CONFIG_TMC9660_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS 500 boot_timeout_ms CONFIG_TMC9660_HARDWARE_RESET n hardware_reset CONFIG_TMC9660_NO_UART_CANARY n uart_canary (inverted) Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} . Both cases are host tests. Next: Porting .

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the TMC9660 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, optionally pulses RSTN ( Config::hardware_reset , needs GpioSet() ), and checks the chip identity in the mode the chip is expected to be in. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds and after a reset the driver detected. No call initialises or resets the chip as a side effect. A call that belongs to another mode returns Error::WrongMode and sends nothing. Every argument is checked against the datasheet tables before a byte is sent; a bad one returns Error::InvalidArgument and sends nothing. A safety guard that says no returns Error::Refused and sends nothing, or leaves the chip as it was. Nothing energises by accident, a stop is never refused, and no write follows a reset the driver could have seen: Safety lists each rule and its test. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read, and a value from a reply that failed its check is discarded ( Error::BadReply , Error::Crc ). Every wait is bounded: the boot wait by Config::boot_timeout_ms (each failed identity poll is charged the 10 ms pause and, on UART, reply_timeout_us , uart_resync_us and the three 5 ms drains it can take), the SPI reply by Config::spi_reply_retries , the UART reply by Config::reply_timeout_us , the PLL by a fixed number of polls. Config{} is the chip's reset configuration. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() makes Config::hardware_reset return Error::Unsupported ; a missing GpioGet() or Log() does nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() always sends the full stop (DRV_EN low, COMMUTATION_MODE 0 or the register-mode zeroes), also after a reported reset or before any start, and then leaves the driver uninitialised. The stop speaks the protocol the driver last proved ( GetMode() ): a failed EnsureInitialized() keeps it. Before any start it is the protocol of Config::mode ; on SPI a parameter-mode stop that reaches a chip in register mode is read by it as a register frame; which registers that frame addresses depends on the register SPI layout (A3: 9-bit offsets in the table, block 1 offset 9 and block 63 offset 0x100; with the wide layout the same bits are MCC offsets 0x104, 0x109 and 0x22b, or RAMDebug 0x300). The datasheet does not say what such a write does, so this is a bench item, not a proved fact. A start of the application whose write fails (a lost, late, corrupt or BUSY reply) is followed as if it happened: the driver adopts the application, or finds the bootloader still answering and stays in it, or leaves the driver uninitialised in the application's protocol. With no proved protocol in bootloader mode and no GpioSet() hook it returns NotInitialized , never a silent Ok . In bootloader mode without a hook it is Ok only when the bootloader still answers its chip type. If it does not (a timeout, a bad frame, a wrong chip type; BUSY, an error status and a seen reset are the bootloader answering and change nothing), the chip may run an application that an unseen restart started: the driver becomes uninitialised, speaks that application's protocol from then on, sends its stop once, best effort, and still returns the error. The application is the one BOOT_MODE names in the configuration read at adoption (nothing was written since the reset, so that is what the OTP loaded, and after a restart the OTP decides) or in the last BlReadConfig() ; with none named it is the protocol of Config::mode . A protocol stop is sent before a UART line is resynchronised, so it is never delayed by Config::uart_resync_us ; the bootloader chip-type check is, after an earlier failed exchange. The stop never returns Ok while the PWM may still be driven: without a GpioSet() hook it also makes sure IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR is 1 (PM "System Off"), and SetParam(IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR, 0) is Refused unless Config::allow_pwm_in_system_off is set. UART Exchange() : a call with tx_len == 0 sends nothing and discards what is waiting on the line (at most rx_len bytes, within timeout_us ); the driver uses it to drain a late reply after a failed exchange, after waiting Config::uart_resync_us . A call with data must discard stale received bytes before it sends. The driver passes its own member buffers, so the bytes live for the whole call. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates tmc9660_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay; optionally RSTN, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN; and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. The public headers include only <algorithm> , <array> , <bit> , <concepts> , <cstddef> , <cstdint> , <limits> , <span> , <type_traits> and <utility> . Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ tmc9660::Error inside tmc9660::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; values from 16 are specific to this driver. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, Deinitialize() ran, or a reset was detected InvalidArgument 2 A Config field or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false or BusStatus::Fault Timeout 4 No reply, the chip did not become ready, or the PLL did not lock DeviceIdMismatch 5 The chip ID is not 0x544D0001 Crc 6 The CRC-8 of a bootloader UART reply does not match Busy 7 The bootloader answered BUSY and the retries ran out DeviceFault 8 A latched error flag forbids the call Unsupported 9 A register offset the SPI layout cannot reach (A3), or hardware_reset without GpioSet() UnexpectedReset 16 The chip reset since the last validated reply; the driver is uninitialised Nack 17 The chip answered with an error status WrongMode 18 The call belongs to another mode than the chip is in Refused 19 A safety guard said no VerifyFailed 20 A read back after a write did not match BadReply 21 A reply failed its checksum, address or opcode check The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config , two 9-byte frame buffers and a few flags: 96 bytes on a 64-bit host ( Config is 44 bytes of it). The frame buffers are members, never locals, so a port that hands them to DMA has them for the whole call. The parameter and register tables are constexpr and live in flash. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ One. The standard's setters take a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None argument; this driver does not: a parameter write is checked by the chip's reply, a register write by the energising guard, and a configuration write by reading it back. The gap is recorded in Ambiguities and unverified items .

Every wait is bounded: the boot wait by Config::boot_timeout_ms (each failed identity poll is charged the 10 ms pause and, on UART, reply_timeout_us , uart_resync_us and the three 5 ms drains it can take), the SPI reply by Config::spi_reply_retries , the UART reply by Config::reply_timeout_us , the PLL by a fixed number of polls. Config{} is the chip's reset configuration. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() makes Config::hardware_reset return Error::Unsupported ; a missing GpioGet() or Log() does nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() always sends the full stop (DRV_EN low, COMMUTATION_MODE 0 or the register-mode zeroes), also after a reported reset or before any start, and then leaves the driver uninitialised. The stop speaks the protocol the driver last proved ( GetMode() ): a failed EnsureInitialized() keeps it. Before any start it is the protocol of Config::mode ; on SPI a parameter-mode stop that reaches a chip in register mode is read by it as a register frame; which registers that frame addresses depends on the register SPI layout (A3: 9-bit offsets in the table, block 1 offset 9 and block 63 offset 0x100; with the wide layout the same bits are MCC offsets 0x104, 0x109 and 0x22b, or RAMDebug 0x300). The datasheet does not say what such a write does, so this is a bench item, not a proved fact. A start of the application whose write fails (a lost, late, corrupt or BUSY reply) is followed as if it happened: the driver adopts the application, or finds the bootloader still answering and stays in it, or leaves the driver uninitialised in the application's protocol. With no proved protocol in bootloader mode and no GpioSet() hook it returns NotInitialized , never a silent Ok . In bootloader mode without a hook it is Ok only when the bootloader still answers its chip type. If it does not (a timeout, a bad frame, a wrong chip type; BUSY, an error status and a seen reset are the bootloader answering and change nothing), the chip may run an application that an unseen restart started: the driver becomes uninitialised, speaks that application's protocol from then on, sends its stop once, best effort, and still returns the error. The application is the one BOOT_MODE names in the configuration read at adoption (nothing was written since the reset, so that is what the OTP loaded, and after a restart the OTP decides) or in the last BlReadConfig() ; with none named it is the protocol of Config::mode . A protocol stop is sent before a UART line is resynchronised, so it is never delayed by Config::uart_resync_us ; the bootloader chip-type check is, after an earlier failed exchange. The stop never returns Ok while the PWM may still be driven: without a GpioSet() hook it also makes sure IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR is 1 (PM "System Off"), and SetParam(IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR, 0) is Refused unless Config::allow_pwm_in_system_off is set. UART Exchange() : a call with tx_len == 0 sends nothing and discards what is waiting on the line (at most rx_len bytes, within timeout_us ); the driver uses it to drain a late reply after a failed exchange, after waiting Config::uart_resync_us . A call with data must discard stale received bytes before it sends. The driver passes its own member buffers, so the bytes live for the whole call.

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state.

docs.text: tmc9660::Error inside tmc9660::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; values from 16 are specific to this driver. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, Deinitialize() ran, or a reset was detected InvalidArgument 2 A Config field or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false or BusStatus::Fault Timeout 4 No reply, the chip did not become ready, or the PLL did not lock DeviceIdMismatch 5 The chip ID is not 0x544D0001 Crc 6 The CRC-8 of a bootloader UART reply does not match Busy 7 The bootloader answered BUSY and the retries ran out DeviceFault 8 A latched error flag forbids the call Unsupported 9 A register offset the SPI layout cannot reach (A3), or hardware_reset without GpioSet() UnexpectedReset 16 The chip reset since the last validated reply; the driver is uninitialised Nack 17 The chip answered with an error status WrongMode 18 The call belongs to another mode than the chip is in Refused 19 A safety guard said no VerifyFailed 20 A read back after a write did not match BadReply 21 A reply failed its checksum, address or opcode check The API guide says what to do about each.
docs.title: Errors

docs.text: No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config , two 9-byte frame buffers and a few flags: 96 bytes on a 64-bit host ( Config is 44 bytes of it). The frame buffers are members, never locals, so a port that hands them to DMA has them for the whole call. The parameter and register tables are constexpr and live in flash.

docs.text: Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver.
docs.title: Platform

docs.text: One. The standard's setters take a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None argument; this driver does not: a parameter write is checked by the chip's reply, a register write by the energising guard, and a configuration write by reading it back. The gap is recorded in Ambiguities and unverified items .

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated TMC9660, through the host port host_tmc9660_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/tmc9660_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest tmc9660_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_tmc9660_port.hpp . docs.text: Hardware ¶ The TMC9660's package, pins, bus settings, timing and power, as the driver uses them. The chip is a 70 V smart gate driver with a servo controller (FOC) in hardware and a buck converter; the driver talks to its processor over SPI or UART, never to the power stage directly. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Package, pins and power-up pin functions: Pin Configurations; Pin Descriptions, p. 11 Supply ranges and the hibernation mode: Power Supply - Electrical Characteristics, p. 17 Pin functions at power-up and the UART and SPI of the bootloader: General-Purpose Input/Output Description, p. 19 Clock, reset, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN: Clock and Control Description, p. 63 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Which pins carry the host link ¶ At power-up the bootloader selects the interface from the first valid command it sees on either bus, and the pin functions below replace the plain GPIO functions of the same pins (datasheet, General-Purpose Input/Output Description). A boot configuration written with BlWriteConfig() can move them. Interface Pins Notes UART GPIO6 (pin 62) is UART_TX, GPIO7 (pin 63) is UART_RX The bootloader detects the baud rate from the first byte, 0x55 SPI GPIO9 (pin 1) MISO, GPIO10 (pin 2) MOSI, GPIO11 (pin 3) SCK, GPIO12 (pin 4) CS0 Mode 3, up to 10 MHz, 40-bit bootloader datagrams The driver is built for one bus per object: a port derives from SpiInterface or from UartInterface , never both (a compile-time check, tests/compile_fail/both_buses.cpp ). Control pins ¶ The driver drives the control pins only through the optional GpioSet() and GpioGet() hooks of your port, with logical levels; the port maps a level to the physical polarity. Pin Hook Meaning of the logical level RSTN (22) GpioSet(CtrlPin::Reset, ...) ACTIVE holds the chip in reset (the pin is low). Used when Config::hardware_reset is set DRV_EN (21) GpioSet(CtrlPin::DrvEn, ...) ACTIVE allows the gate driver outputs (the pin is high) WAKE (19) GpioSet(CtrlPin::Wake, ...) ACTIVE asserts the wake condition; only your own power-down logic uses it FAULTN (20) GpioGet(CtrlPin::Faultn, high) An input: high false means the chip pulls the pin low. Service() reads it A board that wires DRV_EN high or RSTN to a supervisor leaves GpioSet() out. The driver then cannot drop DRV_EN in DisableDrive() ; the chip-side stop (COMMUTATION_MODE 0, or zero enables in register mode) still runs, and the call never fails because the pin hook is missing. Config::hardware_reset without GpioSet() returns Error::Unsupported from EnsureInitialized() . FAULTN is open drain. In the bootloader it signals that the chip is busy bootstrapping or that a severe error stopped the processor (datasheet, Bootloader FAULTN Signaling). In an application it can also pulse when the chip restarts; Config::faultn_is_reset makes Service() treat a low level as a reset (ambiguity A18 in Ambiguities ). Bus settings ¶ Setting Bootloader SPI TMCL SPI Register-mode SPI UART (all three) Mode 3 3 3 8N1 Clock Up to 10 MHz Up to 10 MHz Up to 10 MHz Autobaud after 0x55 ; 115200 is a safe start Bit order MSB first MSB first MSB first LSB first, standard UART Frame 5 bytes 8 bytes, two transfers 6 bytes 8 bytes (bootloader), 9 bytes (TMCL, register) Chip select Low for each frame Low for each frame Low for each frame - Every SPI exchange is one Transfer() call with chip select low for the whole frame. The TMCL SPI reply arrives in the transfer after the command, so a command costs two transfers (see Parameter mode ). The MISO line stays driven after chip select rises (erratum 2) The TMC9660's SPI peripheral does not return MISO to high impedance when chip select is released. With other SPI devices on the same MISO line, hold the chip in reset during their transfers or add the switch the datasheet shows (Errata, Erratum 2). The driver cannot detect this, and GpioSet(CtrlPin::Reset, ...) is the hook for the first workaround. Timing ¶ Parameter Value Driver Power-up or wake to a ready application, self-test on 44 ms typical Config::boot_timeout_ms (500 ms: the datasheet gives a typical value only, A9) Same, self-test off 10.5 ms typical The same wait Wait after a write that reconfigures the chip not specified Config::settle_us (20 ms, A13) Gap between a TMCL SPI command and its reply request not specified Config::spi_gap_us (1 ms) UART reply wait not specified Config::reply_timeout_us (50 ms) The driver waits with your port's DelayUs() ; nothing in it sleeps or spins on a clock of its own. Power ¶ Rail Range Note VSA 7.7 V to 80 V Core and buck supply; the WAKE pin may be shorted to it VS 7.7 V to 70 V Gate driver supply VCC_IO 2.5 V to 5 V (3 V or more for SPI at 10 MHz) Logic levels of the GPIO and of the host link VEXT1, VEXT2 5.0 V, 3.3 V or 2.5 V Outputs, set in the boot configuration; BlWriteConfig() refuses to change them unless allow_ldo_change is set, because both move at once Hibernation ( PowerDown() ) puts everything but the always-on block into reset; the chip restarts after the time given or on a rising edge at WAKE, and the driver reports itself uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() runs again. Reference documents ¶ Every pin, setting and timing on this page cites a document in docs/datasheets.yml ; the driver never contains a vendor PDF, only the revision, date and SHA-256 of the file it was written against. docs.text: At power-up the bootloader selects the interface from the first valid command it sees on either bus, and the pin functions below replace the plain GPIO functions of the same pins (datasheet, General-Purpose Input/Output Description). A boot configuration written with BlWriteConfig() can move them. Interface Pins Notes UART GPIO6 (pin 62) is UART_TX, GPIO7 (pin 63) is UART_RX The bootloader detects the baud rate from the first byte, 0x55 SPI GPIO9 (pin 1) MISO, GPIO10 (pin 2) MOSI, GPIO11 (pin 3) SCK, GPIO12 (pin 4) CS0 Mode 3, up to 10 MHz, 40-bit bootloader datagrams The driver is built for one bus per object: a port derives from SpiInterface or from UartInterface , never both (a compile-time check, tests/compile_fail/both_buses.cpp ).
docs.title: Which pins carry the host link

docs.text: The driver drives the control pins only through the optional GpioSet() and GpioGet() hooks of your port, with logical levels; the port maps a level to the physical polarity. Pin Hook Meaning of the logical level RSTN (22) GpioSet(CtrlPin::Reset, ...) ACTIVE holds the chip in reset (the pin is low). Used when Config::hardware_reset is set DRV_EN (21) GpioSet(CtrlPin::DrvEn, ...) ACTIVE allows the gate driver outputs (the pin is high) WAKE (19) GpioSet(CtrlPin::Wake, ...) ACTIVE asserts the wake condition; only your own power-down logic uses it FAULTN (20) GpioGet(CtrlPin::Faultn, high) An input: high false means the chip pulls the pin low. Service() reads it A board that wires DRV_EN high or RSTN to a supervisor leaves GpioSet() out. The driver then cannot drop DRV_EN in DisableDrive() ; the chip-side stop (COMMUTATION_MODE 0, or zero enables in register mode) still runs, and the call never fails because the pin hook is missing. Config::hardware_reset without GpioSet() returns Error::Unsupported from EnsureInitialized() . FAULTN is open drain. In the bootloader it signals that the chip is busy bootstrapping or that a severe error stopped the processor (datasheet, Bootloader FAULTN Signaling). In an application it can also pulse when the chip restarts; Config::faultn_is_reset makes Service() treat a low level as a reset (ambiguity A18 in Ambiguities ).

docs.text: Setting Bootloader SPI TMCL SPI Register-mode SPI UART (all three) Mode 3 3 3 8N1 Clock Up to 10 MHz Up to 10 MHz Up to 10 MHz Autobaud after 0x55 ; 115200 is a safe start Bit order MSB first MSB first MSB first LSB first, standard UART Frame 5 bytes 8 bytes, two transfers 6 bytes 8 bytes (bootloader), 9 bytes (TMCL, register) Chip select Low for each frame Low for each frame Low for each frame - Every SPI exchange is one Transfer() call with chip select low for the whole frame. The TMCL SPI reply arrives in the transfer after the command, so a command costs two transfers (see Parameter mode ). The MISO line stays driven after chip select rises (erratum 2) The TMC9660's SPI peripheral does not return MISO to high impedance when chip select is released. With other SPI devices on the same MISO line, hold the chip in reset during their transfers or add the switch the datasheet shows (Errata, Erratum 2). The driver cannot detect this, and GpioSet(CtrlPin::Reset, ...) is the hook for the first workaround.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( tmc9660_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc9660.git external/driver-tmc9660 git submodule update --init external/driver-tmc9660 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-tmc9660 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tmc9660::tmc9660 ) tmc9660::tmc9660 is an alias of the tmc9660 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect TMC9660_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver TMC9660_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-tmc9660 -B build-tmc9660 cmake --install build-tmc9660 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( tmc9660 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tmc9660::tmc9660 ) The target is tmc9660::tmc9660 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated tmc9660_version.h go to include/tmc9660/inc/ , the template implementation to include/tmc9660/src/tmc9660.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-tmc9660) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-tmc9660 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc9660.git components/tmc9660 tmc9660 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml tmc9660 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : tmc9660 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc9660.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES tmc9660 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/tmc9660_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into tmc9660_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = tmc9660 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. docs.text: Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do.
docs.title: Mechanization policy

docs.text: Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion.
docs.title: Decision rule

docs.text: A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it.
