docs.text: Parameter mode ¶ In parameter mode the chip's processor runs TMCL, Trinamic's command language, and adds software features on top of the hardware: ramps, fault handling, brake chopper, step/direction, scripts. The driver exposes it as Mode::Parameter : SetParam() , GetParam() and friends. Datasheet sections this page relies on Application modes: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Application Modes, p. 16 TMCL frames over UART and SPI: Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a 0, Communication Interfaces, p. 8 Parameter table: Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a 0, Table 57, Full list of parameters, p. 102 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Frames ¶ Bus Frame Driver UART 9 bytes, LSB first: address, command, type, motor, value (4 bytes), checksum One Exchange() per command SPI 8 bytes: command, type, motor, value (4 bytes), checksum; the reply comes in the next transfer Two Transfer() calls: the command, then a reply request ( FF 00 00 00 00 00 00 FF ) On SPI the reply request is repeated up to Config::spi_reply_retries times while the status says NOT_READY or CHECKSUM_ERROR (ambiguity A5); the command is never sent twice. The first frame after a reset carries 0x0C ( FIRST_CMD ) in the status byte. The driver looks for it on every frame: a command frame, its reply request and the reply of a write probe. When it sees it, the chip restarted since the last validated reply, and the call returns Error::UnexpectedReset without a write following it. The placement of the type bits in the UART frame is ambiguity A2 ( Quirks::tmcl_layout ). By default ( Auto ) the driver reads two flag parameters under each layout at start-up and uses the one the chip answers; if both or neither answer it refuses to start ( Refused ) and no write has been sent. Parameters ¶ inc/tmc9660_params.hpp has the 289 parameters of Table 57 of the Parameter Mode Reference Manual, generated by tools/gen_tables/gen_tables.py (see Testing ). Each row carries the number, name, access (read, write, read/write, write-to-clear), range, reset value, and for coded parameters the allowed values. GetParam() and SetParam() check against that row before any byte is sent: a value outside the range, a coded value that is not allowed, or a motor number above 15 is Error::InvalidArgument , nothing sent; writing a read-only parameter or reading a write-only one is Error::InvalidArgument as well; SetParam(Param::COMMUTATION_MODE, nonzero) is Error::Refused : only EnableDrive() leaves the system on; SetParam(Param::MOTOR_TYPE, ...) is Error::Refused while COMMUTATION_MODE is not zero. ClearFlags() writes a mask to a write-to-clear flag parameter. StoreParams() and FactoryDefault(confirm) run the matching TMCL commands; the second needs confirm true and the system off. Global parameters ( GetGlobal() , SetGlobal() ) are checked against inc/tmc9660_globals.hpp , for example the serial address must be odd. The other TMCL commands ¶ Area Calls Motion EnableDrive() , DisableDrive() , MotorStop() , ReferenceSearchCommand() GPIO SetIo() , GetIo() Debug RamDebug() Scripts ScriptDownload() , ScriptRun() , ScriptStop() , ScriptStep() , ScriptReset() , ScriptStatus() , ScriptReadMem() System PowerDown() , ReturnToBootloader() , DisableSpi1Slave() , GetChipId() , GetVersion() A script runs on the chip with its own authority over the motor. The driver downloads and starts scripts but does not analyse them; see Safety and the coverage table in Datasheet map . Detecting a reset on UART ¶ SPI parameter mode shows a reset in the status byte. UART replies have no such flag, so the driver writes a canary value ( Config::canary_value ) to a user variable ( Config::canary_variable , 15) when it starts and reads it before every write. A different value means the chip restarted, and the write is not sent (ambiguity A7). The check adds one read per write; Config::uart_canary = false turns it off for a link where it is too slow, at the cost of an unseen reset going unnoticed. FAULTN, through Service() , is the second way (A18).

docs.text: Platforms ¶ The driver is MCU-agnostic: inc/ and src/ contain no SDK, RTOS or vendor header. A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_tmc9660_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_tmc9660_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds. The root CMakeLists.txt also covers ESP-IDF: under ESP_PLATFORM it registers the repository as a component (a repository scaffolded without the ESP32 platform adds that branch back from the template when it needs it). Zephyr modules, Arduino library manifests and PlatformIO manifests are added only when a product needs them, and an example is added only together with a CI job that builds it. Add a platform ¶ The add-port skill has the details per MCU. In short: Create examples/<platform>/ with the port ( <platform>_tmc9660_port.hpp ), a small example program and a README with the wiring and the expected output. The folder is self-contained: it carries its own port and builds on its own. Build it in CI: a job in .github/workflows/ that builds the example, needed by the CI gate . A platform that CI does not build is not added. If its build system cannot use the root CMakeLists.txt , add the smallest manifest it needs, and say why in the pull request. Never put platform code in inc/ or src/ . Add a row to the table above and a page section if the platform needs one.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port, on SPI or on UART. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Pin functions at power-up and the UART and SPI of the bootloader: General-Purpose Input/Output Description, p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from tmc9660::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc9660_spi_interface.hpp ) or from tmc9660::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc9660_uart_interface.hpp ), not both. The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the concept AnyPort , so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Bus Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept both yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept SPI yes One full-duplex transfer of len bytes with chip select low for all of them; rx is always given. false on any bus error BusStatus Exchange(const uint8_t* tx, std::size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t rx_len, uint32_t timeout_us) noexcept UART yes Send tx_len bytes without gaps, then receive exactly rx_len bytes within the timeout. BusStatus::Ok , Timeout or Fault . Remove the echo of your own bytes on a shared wire and drive the transceiver direction void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept both yes Wait at least us microseconds. A port without it does not compile bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept both no Drive RSTN, DRV_EN or WAKE at the logical level; false if the pin write failed bool GpioGet(CtrlPin, bool& high) noexcept both no Read FAULTN (or another control pin); false if the read failed void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept both no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The SPI port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tmc9660 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One datagram, CS held low for all `len` bytes. `tx` and `rx` both have `len` bytes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the chip's reply gap and boot times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep chip select low for all len bytes; the chip decodes the frame when it rises. The frames are 5 (bootloader), 8 (parameter mode) and 6 (register mode) bytes. The bus requirements below : mode 3, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing and the retries. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. Idle levels. Chip select high and SCK high (mode 3) before the first transfer, so that the chip never sees a partial frame. The UART port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyUartPort : public tmc9660 :: UartInterface < MyUartPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Throw away stale received bytes, send the request, then wait for exactly `rx_len` bytes. With // `tx_len == 0` send nothing and only drain what is waiting (the driver does this after a failed // exchange). The driver tells timeouts from line faults. tmc9660 :: BusStatus Exchange ( const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len , uint32_t timeout_us ) noexcept { const int r = platform_uart_exchange ( tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len , timeout_us ); if ( r == 0 ) { return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Ok ; } if ( r == 1 ) { return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Timeout ; } return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Fault ; } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the exchange must follow: One call, one request. Send the whole request without a pause between bytes; two documents disagree on how long a gap may be before the chip drops a partial message (ambiguity A6), and a request without gaps avoids the question. Receive exactly rx_len bytes , or report Timeout (nothing arrived) or Fault (framing or overrun). Never return partial data as Ok . 8N1, least significant bit first , at the rate the chip has: it detects the rate of the first bytes (9600 to 250000 at the 40 MHz clock), or the boot configuration sets it. Half duplex. On a shared RS-485 wire, enable the transmitter for the request and the receiver for the reply, and discard the echo. Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the TMC9660 needs from the bus as constexpr values in the two interface headers (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning kSpiMode 3 CPOL 1, CPHA 1 kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 10'000'000 f_SCK max kCsHoldNs 100 SCK edge to chip select change, t_CC kContinuousWord true A datagram is one chip select low period kMinCsHighNs 100 Chip select high between two datagrams kClockPhaseNs 20 SCK low and high time kDataSetupNs 20 Data setup and hold kUartDataBits 8 8N1 kMaxBaudRate 5'000'000 Highest baud rate kTurnaroundUs 1000 Assumed reply wait (ambiguity A19); the port timeout adds the frame time kMaxAutobaudRate 250'000 Highest rate the chip detects at 40 MHz Control pins ¶ GpioSet() takes a CtrlPin and a logical GpioSignal ; the port maps them to the physical level: Pin ACTIVE means The port writes CtrlPin::Reset The chip is held in reset RSTN low CtrlPin::DrvEn The gate driver outputs are allowed DRV_EN high CtrlPin::Wake The wake condition is asserted WAKE high Make the pins idle in their safe state (RSTN released, DRV_EN low) before the first transfer; the driver never assumes it. A hardware reset at start is Config::hardware_reset : Hardware reset at start tmc9660 :: Config WithHardwareReset () { tmc9660 :: Config c {}; c . hardware_reset = true ; // the start pulses RSTN (after DRV_EN low); a port without GpioSet gets Unsupported return c ; } A full port with every hook: A port with every optional hook class FullPort : public tmc9660 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits (the reply gap, boot and PLL times). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: RSTN and DRV_EN on GPIOs. ACTIVE means "asserted": RSTN is active low, DRV_EN active // high. bool GpioSet ( tmc9660 :: CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = ( signal == tmc9660 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); if ( pin == tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: Reset ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kResetGpio , ! active ); } if ( pin == tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: DrvEn ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kDrvEnGpio , active ); } return false ; // WAKE is not wired } // Optional: FAULTN, an open-drain output of the chip. `high` is the pin level. bool GpioGet ( tmc9660 :: CtrlPin pin , bool & high ) noexcept { if ( pin != tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: Faultn ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_read ( kFaultnGpio , high ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( tmc9660 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > tmc9660 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kResetGpio = 7 ; static constexpr int kDrvEnGpio = 8 ; static constexpr int kFaultnGpio = 9 ; }; A GpioSet() that returns void is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check this rule and the others. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_tmc9660_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. docs.text: Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port, on SPI or on UART. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Pin functions at power-up and the UART and SPI of the bootloader: General-Purpose Input/Output Description, p. 19 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from tmc9660::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc9660_spi_interface.hpp ) or from tmc9660::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc9660_uart_interface.hpp ), not both. The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the concept AnyPort , so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use.

docs.text: Method Bus Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept both yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept SPI yes One full-duplex transfer of len bytes with chip select low for all of them; rx is always given. false on any bus error BusStatus Exchange(const uint8_t* tx, std::size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t rx_len, uint32_t timeout_us) noexcept UART yes Send tx_len bytes without gaps, then receive exactly rx_len bytes within the timeout. BusStatus::Ok , Timeout or Fault . Remove the echo of your own bytes on a shared wire and drive the transceiver direction void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept both yes Wait at least us microseconds. A port without it does not compile bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept both no Drive RSTN, DRV_EN or WAKE at the logical level; false if the pin write failed bool GpioGet(CtrlPin, bool& high) noexcept both no Read FAULTN (or another control pin); false if the read failed void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept both no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string

docs.text: my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tmc9660 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One datagram, CS held low for all `len` bytes. `tx` and `rx` both have `len` bytes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the chip's reply gap and boot times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep chip select low for all len bytes; the chip decodes the frame when it rises. The frames are 5 (bootloader), 8 (parameter mode) and 6 (register mode) bytes. The bus requirements below : mode 3, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing and the retries. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. Idle levels. Chip select high and SCK high (mode 3) before the first transfer, so that the chip never sees a partial frame.
docs.title: The SPI port

docs.text: my_port.hpp class MyUartPort : public tmc9660 :: UartInterface < MyUartPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Throw away stale received bytes, send the request, then wait for exactly `rx_len` bytes. With // `tx_len == 0` send nothing and only drain what is waiting (the driver does this after a failed // exchange). The driver tells timeouts from line faults. tmc9660 :: BusStatus Exchange ( const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len , uint32_t timeout_us ) noexcept { const int r = platform_uart_exchange ( tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len , timeout_us ); if ( r == 0 ) { return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Ok ; } if ( r == 1 ) { return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Timeout ; } return tmc9660 :: BusStatus :: Fault ; } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the exchange must follow: One call, one request. Send the whole request without a pause between bytes; two documents disagree on how long a gap may be before the chip drops a partial message (ambiguity A6), and a request without gaps avoids the question. Receive exactly rx_len bytes , or report Timeout (nothing arrived) or Fault (framing or overrun). Never return partial data as Ok . 8N1, least significant bit first , at the rate the chip has: it detects the rate of the first bytes (9600 to 250000 at the 40 MHz clock), or the boot configuration sets it. Half duplex. On a shared RS-485 wire, enable the transmitter for the request and the receiver for the reply, and discard the echo.
docs.title: The UART port

docs.text: The driver states what the TMC9660 needs from the bus as constexpr values in the two interface headers (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning kSpiMode 3 CPOL 1, CPHA 1 kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 10'000'000 f_SCK max kCsHoldNs 100 SCK edge to chip select change, t_CC kContinuousWord true A datagram is one chip select low period kMinCsHighNs 100 Chip select high between two datagrams kClockPhaseNs 20 SCK low and high time kDataSetupNs 20 Data setup and hold kUartDataBits 8 8N1 kMaxBaudRate 5'000'000 Highest baud rate kTurnaroundUs 1000 Assumed reply wait (ambiguity A19); the port timeout adds the frame time kMaxAutobaudRate 250'000 Highest rate the chip detects at 40 MHz
docs.title: Bus requirements

docs.text: GpioSet() takes a CtrlPin and a logical GpioSignal ; the port maps them to the physical level: Pin ACTIVE means The port writes CtrlPin::Reset The chip is held in reset RSTN low CtrlPin::DrvEn The gate driver outputs are allowed DRV_EN high CtrlPin::Wake The wake condition is asserted WAKE high Make the pins idle in their safe state (RSTN released, DRV_EN low) before the first transfer; the driver never assumes it. A hardware reset at start is Config::hardware_reset : Hardware reset at start tmc9660 :: Config WithHardwareReset () { tmc9660 :: Config c {}; c . hardware_reset = true ; // the start pulses RSTN (after DRV_EN low); a port without GpioSet gets Unsupported return c ; } A full port with every hook: A port with every optional hook class FullPort : public tmc9660 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits (the reply gap, boot and PLL times). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: RSTN and DRV_EN on GPIOs. ACTIVE means "asserted": RSTN is active low, DRV_EN active // high. bool GpioSet ( tmc9660 :: CtrlPin pin , tmc9660 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = ( signal == tmc9660 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); if ( pin == tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: Reset ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kResetGpio , ! active ); } if ( pin == tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: DrvEn ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kDrvEnGpio , active ); } return false ; // WAKE is not wired } // Optional: FAULTN, an open-drain output of the chip. `high` is the pin level. bool GpioGet ( tmc9660 :: CtrlPin pin , bool & high ) noexcept { if ( pin != tmc9660 :: CtrlPin :: Faultn ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_read ( kFaultnGpio , high ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( tmc9660 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > tmc9660 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kResetGpio = 7 ; static constexpr int kDrvEnGpio = 8 ; static constexpr int kFaultnGpio = 9 ; }; A GpioSet() that returns void is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check this rule and the others.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then read a parameter from your MCU: wire the chip, write a small port class, call two driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Package, pins and power-up pin functions: Pin Configurations; Pin Descriptions, p. 11 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated TMC9660, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/tmc9660_host_example TMC9660 driver 0.1.0 on the host tmc9660: initialised bootloader: chip type 544D0001 parameter mode: chip type 544D0001 MAX_TORQUE 70000: InvalidArgument drive on, DRV_EN high MAX_TORQUE 1500 drive off, DRV_EN low done: 0 errors The calls in main.cpp take the chip from its bootloader to a running drive and back to off; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ The bootloader listens on UART and SPI at once, on the pins below. Use one bus; the driver is built for one. MCU TMC9660 Notes SPI SCK GPIO11 (pin 3) Mode 3, up to 10 MHz; 1 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI GPIO10 (pin 2) SPI MISO GPIO9 (pin 1) Stays driven after chip select rises (erratum 2): no other SPI device on this line GPIO (chip select) GPIO12 (pin 4) Low for the whole frame: one transfer per frame GPIO RSTN (pin 22) Optional: hardware reset; leave the chip's pull-down alone when unused GPIO DRV_EN (pin 21) Optional for this example; the driver raises it only through the guarded call 3.3 V VCC_IO (pin 9) 2.2 V to 5.5 V; 1 µF to GND close to the pin GND GND (pin 8) Share the ground with the power stage VSA and VS carry the motor supply and the chip's own supplies need their capacitors: Hardware has the full pin list, the reference circuit and the timing. Do not connect a motor for the first steps. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the tmc9660::tmc9660 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc9660.git external/driver-tmc9660 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves bytes. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tmc9660 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One datagram, CS held low for all `len` bytes. `tx` and `rx` both have `len` bytes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the chip's reply gap and boot times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks, the UART variant and the transfer rules. 4. Read a parameter ¶ main.cpp #include "tmc9660.hpp" int read_actual_velocity ( MyPort & port , int32_t & velocity ) { tmc9660 :: Config config {}; config . mode = tmc9660 :: Mode :: Parameter ; // the chip boots into the mode its boot configuration says tmc9660 :: TMC9660 < MyPort > chip ( port , config ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. bus up, identity check, first handshake return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus, Timeout or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring and mode } const auto v = chip . GetParam ( tmc9660 :: Param :: ACTUAL_VELOCITY ); // 2. a checked read of one parameter if ( ! v ) { return static_cast < int > ( v . error ); // UnexpectedReset: the chip restarted, start again } velocity = static_cast < int32_t > ( v . value ); // 3. in the unit of the parameter return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , and checks the chip identity in the mode you named. It does not reset the chip unless Config::hardware_reset is set: it adopts the chip as it is. GetParam() checks the parameter and the motor number, then runs one TMCL command. The value is in the unit of the parameter, as Table 57 of the Parameter Mode Reference Manual defines it. A chip that has just powered up is in its bootloader: start with Config::mode = Mode::Bootloader and BlStartApplication() ( Bootloader ) to reach parameter mode, as the host example does. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() : the bus did not come up EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch The mode (the chip may be in its bootloader), the wiring and the device address ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns Timeout VCC_IO and RSTN: the chip never answered A call returns WrongMode The chip is in another mode than Config::mode says EnableDrive() returns DeviceFault A latched error flag: read GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS and GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS , fix the cause, clear them Next ¶ API guide : start the application, set parameters, drive, handle errors. Safety : what keeps the power stage off. Configuration : every Config field, the readings of ambiguous documents, Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the MCU examples. Platforms : which MCUs have a port and an example.

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. Guards no test kills (surviving mutants) 6 review test RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules 3 review test RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI 4 CI lint RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing 6 review review RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit 3 review review RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard 3 test test RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read 2 review test RD-32 Docs style: line length, merged bullets, stale text 3 lint lint RD-33 Another project's name or dated history 1 lint lint RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check 3 lint lint Chip-protocol and safety classes ¶ RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check ¶ Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up). RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"

Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
