docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up).
docs.title: RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).
docs.title: RD-11 Header outside the library subset

docs.text: Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != .
docs.title: RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic

docs.text: Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests .
docs.title: RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses

docs.text: Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned).
docs.title: RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended.
docs.title: RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp .
docs.title: RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ

docs.text: Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?"
docs.title: RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type

docs.text: Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision.
docs.title: RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2

docs.text: Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call.
docs.title: RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete

docs.text: Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?"
docs.title: RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults

docs.text: Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert .
docs.title: RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler

docs.text: Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA

docs.text: Register mode ¶ In register mode the application exposes the hardware registers directly, with none of the parameter-mode software. The driver exposes it as Mode::Register : ReadReg() , WriteReg() , UpdateReg() and GateDriverStart() . Datasheet sections this page relies on Application modes: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Application Modes, p. 16 Protections and the fault pin: Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1, Protections Description, p. 56 Register-mode SPI and UART datagrams: Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a 0, Communication interfaces, p. 8 Register map: Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a 0, Register Map, p. 57 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Frames ¶ Bus Frame Driver UART 9 bytes, with the register address, a write or read code (146, 148, 142), data and a checksum One Exchange() SPI 6 bytes: block, offset, write bit, data (4 bytes); the reply to a datagram arrives with the next one A read is two Transfer() calls (request, then a harmless fetch); a write is three (a probe read comes first) On SPI every reply starts with a boot bit and a 3-bit datagram counter. The first reply after a reset has the boot bit set, and it is the baseline EnsureInitialized() takes. The driver checks both on every later reply: a set boot bit, or a counter that skips a number, means the chip restarted or a datagram was lost, and the call returns Error::UnexpectedReset . A write is preceded by a probe datagram (a read of MCC_INFO_CHIP ), so that a restart is seen before the write is sent, not after it. The SPI register layout has a 9-bit offset (ambiguity A3), but 8 registers lie above offset 0x1FF . In the table layout these return Error::Unsupported ; Quirks::reg_spi_wide_offset selects the 10-bit layout and reaches all 163. UART reaches all of them. The bit order of the UART fields is A4. Registers ¶ inc/tmc9660_registers.hpp has 163 registers generated from the Register Mode Reference Manual: block, offset, access, writable mask, reset value, and in the fields::<register> namespaces the bit fields. ReadReg() and WriteReg() reject an address that is not in the table, a write to a read-only register, and a write that touches bits outside the writable mask ( Error::InvalidArgument , nothing sent). UpdateReg(addr, mask, value) reads, changes the masked bits and writes back. Starting the gate driver ¶ The gate driver of the TMC9660 can switch a motor's power stage. WriteReg() and UpdateReg() therefore refuse any write that would turn it on: the energising bits of MCC_GDRV_HW (mask 0x0300'080F ) and of MCC_PWM_CONFIG (mask 0x0000'FF07 ) return Error::Refused . A stop is not refused: writing zero to them is allowed. GateDriverStart(GateDriverRegConfig) is the one way on. It works in this order: It checks the mode and the configuration before any byte is sent: every value inside the register's writable mask, the chop value 1 to 7 ( Error::InvalidArgument , nothing sent). It reads MCC_GDRV_STATUS and MCC_GDRV_FAULT before anything is written or cleared. A latched status bit (the bootstrap flags excepted) or an active fault or undervoltage is Error::DeviceFault and the evidence stays in the chip for you to read and clear. It writes the configuration with nothing energised (PWM enables with CHOP 1, gate current, timing, break-before- make, MCC_GDRV_PROT , the overcurrent words), writes zero to the status enable register and clears the status flags, then reads status and fault again: a condition that latches again is Error::DeviceFault . Only then it raises DRV_EN, writes MCC_GDRV_HW , reads it back ( Error::VerifyFailed on a difference) and writes the PWM enables with the chop value last. After the bootstrap wait ( Config::settle_us ) it writes MCC_GDRV_STATUS_EN and MCC_GDRV_PROT_EN (the manual's protection setup; defaults 0xEFFFFFFF and 0xAFFFFFFF in GateDriverRegConfig ) and reads both back ( Error::VerifyFailed ). Without them a shorted bridge would be neither reported nor shut off by the chip. A fault, a failed write or a read-back that differs makes the driver write zero to the enables ( DisableDrive() ) before it returns. DisableDrive() in register mode writes zero to MCC_GDRV_HW and MCC_PWM_CONFIG , writes again after a reported reset, and reads both back ( Error::VerifyFailed if an energising bit is still set). Detecting a reset on UART ¶ UART register mode has no reset indication in the reply. The driver reads MCC_INFO_CHIP at start and otherwise relies on FAULTN through Service() (A18). This is the weakest reset detection of the driver and is listed under not verified .

DisableDrive() in register mode writes zero to MCC_GDRV_HW and MCC_PWM_CONFIG , writes again after a reported reset, and reads both back ( Error::VerifyFailed if an energising bit is still set).

docs.text: UART register mode has no reset indication in the reply. The driver reads MCC_INFO_CHIP at start and otherwise relies on FAULTN through Service() (A18). This is the weakest reset detection of the driver and is listed under not verified .

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: Safety ¶ The TMC9660 can energise a motor's power stage: 70 V and amperes. This page lists what the driver does so that a bug in your application, a lost reply or a chip that restarted cannot turn the gate driver on by surprise, and what it does not cover. Each rule is a test in tests/test_safety.cpp , tests/test_parameter.cpp or tests/test_register.cpp , and each guard has a mutant that the tests must kill (see Testing ). Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Supply ranges and the hibernation mode: Power Supply - Electrical Characteristics, p. 17 Protections and the fault pin: Protections Description, p. 56 Clock, reset, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN: Clock and Control Description, p. 63 Boot configuration list, LDO and bootstrap configuration: Bootloader, Configuration, p. 83 Errata (OTP_BURN workaround, SPI slave MISO): Errata, p. 99 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The rules ¶ Rule How the driver keeps it Nothing energises by accident Parameter mode: only EnableDrive() leaves COMMUTATION_MODE at a non-zero value (a stored script excepted: see below); SetParam() refuses it ( Refused ). Register mode: WriteReg() and UpdateReg() refuse the energising bits of MCC_GDRV_HW and MCC_PWM_CONFIG ; only GateDriverStart() sets them The guards complete before the energising write EnableDrive() reads GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS and GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS first ( DeviceFault if either is non-zero), raises DRV_EN, and only then writes COMMUTATION_MODE ; when that write fails (the chip may have run it all the same) it runs the full stop of DisableDrive() . GateDriverStart() reads GDRV_STATUS and GDRV_FAULT before it clears anything (a latched bit is DeviceFault and the evidence stays), writes the protection words, clears, reads again, and only then raises DRV_EN. After the bootstrap wait it writes GDRV_STATUS_EN and GDRV_PROT_EN and reads them back ( VerifyFailed ), so a shorted bridge is reported and shut off by the chip. It then reads the latched evidence once more: a protection that trips at once (for example with the default overcurrent words of 0, the lowest threshold with no blanking, and every protection on) makes the start DeviceFault and the stage is switched off again. Set gdrv_ocp_uvw and gdrv_ocp_y2 for the board A stop is never refused DisableDrive() and Deinitialize() always send the full stop (also after a reported reset or before any start): DisableDrive() drops DRV_EN first, then writes COMMUTATION_MODE 0 (parameter mode) or zero to MCC_GDRV_HW and MCC_PWM_CONFIG (register mode), in the protocol the driver last proved: Config::mode before any start, the started application after BlStartApplication() , and a failed restart keeps it. In bootloader mode without a successful start and without a GpioSet() hook the driver cannot know what the chip runs: the stop returns NotInitialized instead of Ok ; with the bootloader adopted and no hook, the stop asks the bootloader for its chip type (with the SPI reset evidence checked) and is Ok only when it answers; when it does not, the driver sends the stop of the application the last BOOT_MODE read named (or Config::mode ), becomes uninitialised in that protocol and returns the error, so this and later stops reach a running application. A start write of the boot-mode word that fails other than by a bootloader error status, and any write of that word with START_MOTOR_CTRL set (A24), is followed as a start: the driver adopts the application, or confirms the bootloader still runs, or stays uninitialised in the application's protocol, so a later stop speaks to what may be running. It runs in any mode, after an unseen reset, without the canary check, and when a step fails it still runs the next. MotorStop() is not gated by a probe either. A parameter-mode stop or MotorStop() that fails for any reason (a reported reset, a lost frame, a stale or late UART reply, a frame merged with a partial request) is sent once more after the line is resynchronised, then the IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR check runs; a failed write of the register-mode stop is repeated once, and the register-mode stop reads both words back ( VerifyFailed if one still has an energising bit). On a UART line that is out of step the stop is sent first and the line is resynchronised afterwards, so a parameter-mode or register-mode stop is not delayed by uart_resync_us (the bootloader check below is an ordinary request and waits for it) System off really switches the PWM off PM "System Off": with IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR (parameter 9, stored) at 0 the PWM stays active when COMMUTATION_MODE is 0. On a port with a GpioSet() hook the dropped DRV_EN switches the stage off. On a port without it the parameter-mode stop reads parameter 9, sets it to 1 and enters System off again when it was 0, and reads it back; a stop that cannot establish this returns an error ( VerifyFailed or the bus error), never Ok while the PWM may still be driven. SetParam(IDLE_MOTOR_PWM_BEHAVIOR, 0) is Refused unless Config::allow_pwm_in_system_off is set (the stop without a DRV_EN hook sets it to 1 whatever that says) No write after a reset the driver did not see Every transport checks the reset evidence of its bus on each reply (see below). A write is only sent after a probe or canary check passed; a write the chip may have lost returns UnexpectedReset and the driver is uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() succeeds again. PowerDown() and ReturnToBootloader() stop first; when that stop saw a reset they return UnexpectedReset and send nothing more (no power-down command, no Boot ) Nothing is sent on a bad argument Range, access, motor number, mask, address and alignment are checked against the generated tables first: InvalidArgument , zero transfers ( tests/test_safety.cpp ) Boot with the drive on is impossible ReturnToBootloader() switches the drive off, reads COMMUTATION_MODE back, and sends Boot only when it reads 0 (erratum 3). A chip that acknowledges the stop but stays on gets Refused and no Boot Reconfiguring the motor needs the system off SetParam(MOTOR_TYPE) and FactoryDefault() are Refused while COMMUTATION_MODE is not 0; FactoryDefault() also needs confirm Configuration cannot start an unsafe application BlWriteConfig() refuses a start with a reserved boot mode or a clock other than 40 MHz, refuses an LDO change without allow_ldo_change , writes the boot-mode word last, verifies by reading back, and waits for the PLL The OTP is never written BlWrite32(Bank::Otp, ...) is Refused ; OTP_BURN is not exposed Transfer buffers belong to the driver The 9-byte and 8-byte frame buffers are members of the object, so the bytes live as long as the call; a test checks that the port is given addresses inside the object The frame layout is proved before a write At start-up in parameter mode the driver reads two flag parameters under each TMCL layout (A2); no write leaves before exactly one layout answers, otherwise Refused A late reply cannot answer the next request After a UART failure the next exchange first waits Config::uart_resync_us and drains the line (a drain that fails itself leaves the line dirty and the call returns Bus without sending); a reply with a wrong operation, address or host is BadReply and marks the line dirty again Reset evidence by transport ¶ Transport How an unseen reset shows What the driver does Bootloader SPI The status of a reply is SESSION_START or BOOTLOADER_RESUMED UnexpectedReset , uninitialised Bootloader UART No indicator; FAULTN is the only evidence ( Service() , A18) Not detected without the pin; the bank is selected again before every word written, so a restart between words cannot send a word to the flash bank Parameter SPI FIRST_CMD (0x0C) in the status byte of a frame UnexpectedReset ; checked on the command frame, its reply request and the write probe Parameter UART The canary variable (A7); Service() also sees WATCHDOG_EVENT in GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS when it was not set at the start The write is not sent; UnexpectedReset Register SPI The boot bit or a skipped datagram counter UnexpectedReset Register UART No indicator; FAULTN, checked before every write when faultn_is_reset is set UnexpectedReset and no frame; not detected without the pin The Not-detected rows are a limit of the chip's replies, not of the driver; see Ambiguities and unverified items . A noisy SPI line can corrupt the one status byte that carries FIRST_CMD ; the fuzz target documents this as residual risk. What the driver does not cover ¶ Scripts. A TMCL script downloaded with ScriptDownload() runs on the chip and can set parameters. The driver refuses a script that contains SAP of COMMUTATION_MODE with a non-zero value or AAP of it ( Refused , nothing sent), but it does not analyse anything else, and ScriptRun() starts whatever the chip already holds. The power stage. Wrong MOSFET or motor data, a shorted bridge or an overcurrent setting that is too high are outside the driver. The chip's own protections (overcurrent, VGS, undervoltage, thermal) are configured by you and watched by the flag guards above only at the moment of starting. Hardware not wired. Without the GpioSet() hook the driver cannot drop DRV_EN; a board that needs a hardware stop must wire DRV_EN to something that can. Concurrency. The driver is not thread-safe. Call DisableDrive() from the same context as the other calls, or guard the object with one mutex; the stop path itself needs no more than the port's own hooks. Verification on hardware. Everything here is verified against a model of the chip built from the documents ( Testing ); nothing has run on a real TMC9660 yet. Document Revision Get it Datasheet: TMC9660 70V Smart Gate Driver with Servo (FOC) Controller in HW and Buck Converter (Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926) 1, 2024-11 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Parameter Mode Reference Manual (Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a) 0, 2025-02 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Register Mode Reference Manual (Analog Devices (Trinamic) n/a) 0, 2025-04 vendor page Datasheet: TMC9660 Configuration and Bootstrapping (Analog Devices (Trinamic) AN-2601) 0, 2025-01-08 vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the chip, safety tests that assert on the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, one-edit mutants of every guard, generated and formatted tables, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Nothing here has run on a real chip. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the TMC9660: the bootloader with its configuration memory and flash, parameter mode over SPI and UART, register mode over SPI and UART, resets, and injected faults. They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DTMC9660_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure The unit tests are 206 cases in one executable ( tmc9660_host_tests ); the other CTest entries are listed below. File Covers tests/test_frames.cpp Every frame encoder and decoder against the documents' worked examples, and the CRC-8 tests/test_bootloader.cpp Bootloader over SPI and UART: info, memory, configuration write, start, erase, delayed replies, PLL tests/test_parameter.cpp Parameter mode: ranges, access, coded values, globals, scripts, resets on SPI and UART tests/test_register.cpp Register mode: access, masks, the energising guard, GateDriverStart() , the datagram counter tests/test_safety.cpp The rules of Safety , each asserted on the chip's record of what happened to it tests/test_gate_driver.cpp GateDriverStart() : the latched-evidence masks bit by bit, CHOP 1 before the enable, the bootstrap wait, a trip after the protections, every failure ends switched off tests/test_hardening.cpp Reply validation, scripts that set COMMUTATION_MODE , WATCHDOG_EVENT , bootloader SPI BUSY and dead lines tests/test_stop_paths.cpp The stop after an unseen reset on SPI and UART, parameter and register mode; The last full run killed 167 of 167. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( tmc9660_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/tmc9660.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. It passes when the report passes: a finding of a mandatory or required guideline that no record deviates, a scan problem or a suppression error fails; advisory findings are warnings. Each blocking finding is listed as file:line failure Rule message . The SARIF, JSON and CSV reports and the full log are kept in $PREFLIGHT_OUT/misra (default $TMPDIR/kokeb-preflight/<repository>-<time> ). esp32 builds what ru-build.yml builds: the matrix of examples/esp32/app_config.yml (the submodule's generate_matrix.py ), every app and build type with build_app.sh , on ESP-IDF release/v5.5 for the target of the examples. An app listed for another ESP-IDF version or target is not built in the image; the last line names it. The CodeQL CLI and the pinned Arm toolchain exist for Linux x86-64 only. On an arm64 host (Apple silicon) the MISRA image is linux/amd64 and runs emulated; the ESP32 image is native on both architectures. A host without Docker cannot run either; tools/preflight.sh then names both as skipped. Differences from CI to know: the ESP-IDF commit is pinned in Dockerfile.esp32 (CI clones the tip of the release branch each run) and the ESP32 image uses Ubuntu's Python 3.12; the MISRA image has Ubuntu's cmake and ninja where the runner has newer ones. MISRA_ARGS=--host-only scans the host build only, which is faster and leaves the Cortex-M preprocessor paths to CI. Bumping the pins ¶ Dockerfile.misra : CI_TOOLS_REF is the commit ru-misra.yml@v1 resolves to ( git ls-remote https://github.com/kokeb-labs/ci-tools v1 ), HANDBOOK_REF the default handbook_ref of that workflow; the tool versions follow from toolchain.json of that commit. Dockerfile.esp32 : IDF_COMMIT is the commit CI prints as ESP-IDF release/v5.5 is <sha> . Rebuild with docker rmi kokeb-ci-misra:local kokeb-ci-esp32:local , then run --container . Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target tmc9660_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ Nothing in this repository has run on a chip. An MCU example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it starts the chip, reads its identity and its actual velocity twice a second. The bench steps that settle each reading of Ambiguities are open work: start with A2, A3 and A4 (the frame layouts), then the reset evidence of UART register mode. Record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

docs.text: A first push is green only when the two CI checks a workstation used to leave to CI have passed locally. tools/preflight.sh --container runs them in Docker, in addition to everything else it runs, and its last lines are == N failure(s) and the gates line; both must show 0 failures. misra runs the ru-misra workflow's own scripts ( tools/ci-container/misra.sh , image tools/ci-container/Dockerfile.misra ): the caller's inputs are read from .github/workflows/ci-misra.yml ; the tools are the versions and SHA-256 hashes of tools/misra/toolchain.json of the pinned ci-tools commit (CodeQL CLI bundle, codeql/misra-cpp-coding-standards pack, Arm GNU toolchain, clang-tidy, cppcheck); the configure, traced build, analysis, deviation records and report are the CI's. It passes when the report passes: a finding of a mandatory or required guideline that no record deviates, a scan problem or a suppression error fails; advisory findings are warnings. Each blocking finding is listed as file:line failure Rule message . The SARIF, JSON and CSV reports and the full log are kept in $PREFLIGHT_OUT/misra (default $TMPDIR/kokeb-preflight/<repository>-<time> ). esp32 builds what ru-build.yml builds: the matrix of examples/esp32/app_config.yml (the submodule's generate_matrix.py ), every app and build type with build_app.sh , on ESP-IDF release/v5.5 for the target of the examples. An app listed for another ESP-IDF version or target is not built in the image; the last line names it. The CodeQL CLI and the pinned Arm toolchain exist for Linux x86-64 only. On an arm64 host (Apple silicon) the MISRA image is linux/amd64 and runs emulated; the ESP32 image is native on both architectures. A host without Docker cannot run either; tools/preflight.sh then names both as skipped. Differences from CI to know: the ESP-IDF commit is pinned in Dockerfile.esp32 (CI clones the tip of the release branch each run) and the ESP32 image uses Ubuntu's Python 3.12; the MISRA image has Ubuntu's cmake and ninja where the runner has newer ones. MISRA_ARGS=--host-only scans the host build only, which is faster and leaves the Cortex-M preprocessor paths to CI.
docs.title: Rehearsing the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds locally

docs.text: Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target tmc9660_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts.
docs.title: Documentation snippets

docs.text: Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 .

docs.text: Nothing in this repository has run on a chip. An MCU example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it starts the chip, reads its identity and its actual velocity twice a second. The bench steps that settle each reading of Ambiguities are open work: start with A2, A3 and A4 (the frame layouts), then the reset evidence of UART register mode. Record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.
docs.title: On hardware

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Find the cause of an error from the driver, by the call that returned it. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) 19-101926 1: Clock, reset, DRV_EN, WAKE and FAULTN: Clock and Control Description, p. 63 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: either EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus pins in your port against the board ( Hardware ). With a logic analyser, check that the first frame appears on the bus, with chip select low for the whole frame. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ The chip identity did not read 0x544D0001 . The chip answered with something else, or in another protocol. Read value Likely cause Fix 0x00 MISO not connected, or chip select not reaching the chip Check MISO and chip select continuity 0xFF MISO floating high, or the chip unpowered Check VCC_IO, VSA and the supplies; check MISO is not pulled up hard An identity read of another mode Config::mode does not match the chip's boot configuration The chip is in its bootloader ( Mode::Bootloader ), or already in an application Anything else Wrong SPI mode, a shifted bit, or the wrong UART address Use SPI mode 3; check the UART device address is odd and matches EnsureInitialized returns Timeout ¶ The chip did not answer within boot_timeout_ms . Check the supplies, that RSTN is released (or released by your GpioSet() with GpioSignal::INACTIVE ), and FAULTN: low means the chip is busy bootstrapping or reports a severe error such as an undervoltage on the 1.8 V rail. EnsureInitialized returns Unsupported or InvalidArgument ¶ Unsupported : hardware_reset is set but the port has no GpioSet() . InvalidArgument : the configuration is out of range, or the UART device address is even in parameter or register mode ( Configuration ). A call returns WrongMode ¶ The call belongs to another mode than the chip is in; nothing was sent. After BlStartApplication() the driver follows the chip into the new mode on its own. If you started the application by other means, create a driver with the right Config::mode . EnableDrive returns DeviceFault ¶ GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS or GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS has a latched bit. Read them with GetParam() , find the cause (undervoltage, overcurrent, gate-driver fault), fix it, and clear the flags with ClearFlags() . The driver does not clear them for you. A call returns Refused ¶ A safety guard said no, and nothing was sent or changed. The text logged by Log() says which one; the guards are on the Safety page. The usual ones: SetParam(COMMUTATION_MODE, ...) (use EnableDrive() ), a write of MOTOR_TYPE or FactoryDefault() while the system is on (call DisableDrive() first), a register write with an energising bit (use GateDriverStart() ), a configuration that would start with the wrong clock. A call returns UnexpectedReset ¶ The driver saw evidence that the chip restarted since the last reply it trusted: a brown-out, the watchdog, or your own reset. The driver is uninitialised again and sent no write after the evidence. Find out why the chip restarted (supply, GENERAL_STATUS_FLAGS after the restart), then call EnsureInitialized() and configure the chip again. DisableDrive returns an error in bootloader mode without a DRV_EN hook ¶ Without a GpioSet() hook the driver checks that the bootloader still answers before it calls a stop done. When it does not, an unseen restart may have started an application: the driver sends that application's stop (the one BOOT_MODE names in the configuration read at adoption or the last BlReadConfig() , or Config::mode ; BUSY, an error status and a seen reset are the bootloader answering, so they cause no such stop), marks itself uninitialised and speaks that protocol from then on, so DisableDrive() again reaches the application. To recover, call EnsureInitialized() : it starts from Config::mode , so use a Config in the mode the chip boots into, or reset the chip into the bootloader. A reply fails: Crc, BadReply, Busy ¶ Crc and BadReply are single corrupted frames on the bus: lower the clock, shorten the wires, add a ground next to the clock line; the value was discarded. A Crc on every bootloader UART reply points at the CRC-8 reading (A1, Quirks::crc8_reflect_output ). Busy means the bootloader was still working; raise spi_reply_retries . Register reads of some registers return Unsupported ¶ On SPI with the default layout, registers above offset 0x1FF cannot be addressed (A3). Use UART, or set Quirks::reg_spi_wide_offset once a bench check shows the chip uses the wide layout. Another SPI device on the same bus misbehaves ¶ The TMC9660's MISO is not released when chip select rises (erratum 2). Hold the chip in reset during the other device's transfers, or add the switch the datasheet shows ( Hardware ).

Inside the TMC9660 ¶ Inside the TMC9660 Figure description and sources The TMC9660's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.
